exact.reason: Business takeaway: test accuracy paired with the test baseline, repeated CV with its own baseline
exact.before: **1. Prioritise Premium Foodies.** They are 27% of diners but 36% of estimated monthly revenue (AED 872 per diner, the highest), yet only 52% reorder. 101 of 130 sit in the uncertain 25–75% probability band, holding AED 88,385 of monthly spend — the value retention spend can most realistically move. Family Feasters churn most (85%), but 119 of 150 are already below 25%, so they warrant a selective, low-cost win-back; Budget Students (98% reorder) should be served efficiently with less discounting. **2. Promote segment-specific bundles:** Miso Soup + Sushi → Green Tea for Premium Foodies (92% confidence, lift 3.9) and Cola + Dessert + Pizza → Garlic Bread as a family 'pizza night' set (95%, lift 4.8). **3. Use the reorder model as a weekly risk ranking:** it is 86% accurate in repeated cross-validation (90% on the held-out test split) vs a 59% majority baseline, with ROC-AUC 0.94. Score every adult diner weekly, rank the 205 below 50% reorder probability by *expected value* of an offer (probability × spend × margin − cost) rather than probability alone, and treat recency as the early-warning signal. **4. Next step:** run an A/B test stratified by segment (randomised hold-out in each) of the premium-bundle and family win-back offers. Its measured success rates replace the planning assumptions and decide how the retention budget is split between Premium Foodies and Family Feasters.
exact.after: **1. Prioritise Premium Foodies.** They are 27% of diners but 36% of estimated monthly revenue (AED 872 per diner, the highest), yet only 52% reorder. 101 of 130 sit in the uncertain 25–75% probability band, holding AED 88,385 of monthly spend — the value retention spend can most realistically move. Family Feasters churn most (85%), but 119 of 150 are already below 25%, so they warrant a selective, low-cost win-back; Budget Students (98% reorder) should be served efficiently with less discounting. **2. Promote segment-specific bundles:** Miso Soup + Sushi → Green Tea for Premium Foodies (92% confidence, lift 3.9) and Cola + Dessert + Pizza → Garlic Bread as a family 'pizza night' set (95%, lift 4.8). **3. Use the reorder model as a weekly risk ranking:** on the untouched 92-diner test set it is 90.2% accurate (bootstrap 95% CI 83.7%–95.7%) vs a 58.7% majority baseline on the same diners, with ROC-AUC 0.97; in a post-selection stability check (repeated cross-validation on all adult diners) the same configuration averages 85.8% ± 3.0% vs that exercise's 58.5% baseline. Score every adult diner weekly, rank the 205 below 50% reorder probability by *expected value* of an offer (probability × spend × margin − cost) rather than probability alone, and treat recency as the early-warning signal. **4. Next step:** run an A/B test stratified by segment (randomised hold-out in each) of the premium-bundle and family win-back offers. Its measured success rates replace the planning assumptions and decide how the retention budget is split between Premium Foodies and Family Feasters.
